handoff.purpose: Defines the KairosScheduler class and related dataclasses for bounded task scheduling and dispatch.

claims.text: Kairos never talks to the user, never decides trust, and bounces anything that belongs to the senior crew back to the trusted orchestration layer.
claims.why: The chunk defines the scheduler but does not contain code that enforces these claims globally; they refer to the overall system design.

claims.text: Adam owns trust, safety, and the senior Claude crew. He hands Ikarus only the work he has already cleared as low-risk and offloadable.
claims.why: Adam and Ikarus are not defined in this chunk; the claim refers to external roles.

claims.text: Ikarus then: dynamically spawns local workers from a bounded pool, briefs each with a scoped task + the owning specialist's domain, enforces their reduced rights, returns a consolidated report for Adam / the owning specialist to review.
claims.why: This describes behavior of Ikarus, which is not implemented in this chunk; the methods here (accept, dispatch) are part of that, but the full claim is uncheckable.

claims.text: FREE_LANES = ('ollama', 'deepseek', 'codex_cli') — 'Free' means free of CLAUDE tokens: ollama is truly free/local; deepseek and codex_cli are external and spend their own (cheap/subscription) budget.
claims.why: The constant is defined exactly as claimed; the comment explains the meaning.

claims.text: DEFAULT_AVAILABILITY = {'claude_cli': True, 'ollama': True, 'deepseek': False, 'codex_cli': False} — Default posture: local bench on, external benches dormant (no DeepSeek key, Codex only when the CLI is detected by doctor at dispatch time).
claims.why: The constant is defined as claimed; the comment explains the default posture.

claims.text: _paths_overlap: Diagnostic overlap among declared write hints. This is not a proof of write isolation: an agent may touch an undeclared path.
claims.why: The function checks overlap of declared write paths; the docstring accurately states its limitation.

claims.text: max_parallel_writes: Concurrency cap SPECIFICALLY for gate_concurrent_writes, independent of max_workers. Deliberately conservative and separately configurable: every concurrent write-mode offload() triggers a FULL structcore re-index, and that cache's single-flight lock is keyed by RESOLVED ROOT — so N worktrees, N distinct roots, N UNSHARED full re-index builds competing for CPU/RAM at once.
claims.why: The claim references structcore and cached_index which are not defined in this chunk; the attribute exists but its behavior depends on external code.

claims.text: accept: Only low-risk work that Adam would offload is taken; anything that routes back to Claude is bounced to Adam.
claims.why: The method uses route_and_select to decide; the routing logic is not in this chunk. The claim about 'low-risk' and 'Adam' is uncheckable.

claims.text: plan: Dry run: who gets spawned, in how many bounded waves.
claims.why: The method calls accept and calculates waves based on max_workers; it returns a plan without executing.

claims.text: dispatch: Sequential by default (parallel=False): each live write is verified by diffing a WHOLE-repo content-hash snapshot around that one run (offload._repo_snapshot), which catches even writes outside --paths -- but two such runs on one repo concurrently would cross-attribute disk_changed.
claims.why: The claim references offload._repo_snapshot which is not defined in this chunk; the behavior is uncheckable.

claims.text: dispatch: Writable concurrency stays sequential with whole-repository snapshots until Forge gives every attempt its own workcell/worktree.
claims.why: The code enforces sequential execution for writes when parallel=True and has_writes is True (can_parallel = parallel and not has_writes). The claim is consistent with the code.

claims.text: dispatch: Pairwise-disjoint declared strings are not evidence that agentic writers stay within those strings.
claims.why: The comment in the code states this explicitly; the method does not rely on declared path disjointness for safety.

claims.text: dispatch: The hazard this closes is not misattribution — it is destruction: every offload() gets a fresh provider whose rollback snapshot is per-call while the FILES are shared, so if task A's verify fails after task B landed a verified write to the same file, A's rollback writes its own stale pre-run bytes over B's finished work, with no error raised.
claims.why: The claim describes behavior of offload and rollback which are not in this chunk; the hazard analysis is uncheckable.

claims.text: dispatch: Separate checkouts remove that by construction rather than by convention: `isolate_paths` and disjoint declared paths never could, because an agentic writer is not bound by the strings it was handed.
claims.why: The claim references separate checkouts and isolate_paths which are not implemented in this chunk; the behavior is uncheckable.

claims.text: dispatch: The isolation now EXISTS — see gate_concurrent_writes() below, which runs each write through daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt (its own worktree, its own hardened patch capture) fanned out concurrently, and daedalus.kairos.gated_writes.promote_candidates(), which lands gated candidates one at a time behind a cross-process lock with cumulative re-gating.
claims.why: References external modules (daedalus.spine.attempt, daedalus.kairos.gated_writes) not present in this chunk.

claims.text: dispatch: dispatch() keeps its existing auto-land contract for a single write (offload() has always auto-landed a sequential one), and does not silently switch write-mode dispatch to the gated-candidate shape — that is a product decision.
claims.why: The code does not call gate_concurrent_writes or promote_candidates; it uses offload directly. The claim is consistent.

claims.text: gate_concurrent_writes: Safe concurrent WRITE dispatch: PHASE 1 only (gating, not landing). Returns one GatedCandidate per accepted write task.
claims.why: The method is incomplete in this chunk (truncated); the claim cannot be verified.

claims.text: gate_concurrent_writes: Every write task runs CONCURRENTLY, each through TaskAttempt in its own worktree.
claims.why: References TaskAttempt and worktree isolation not present in this chunk.

claims.text: gate_concurrent_writes: The primary checkout at repo_root is NEVER touched by this call — that is TaskAttempt's own structural guarantee (see tests/test_spine_attempt.py::test_happy_path_artifact_and_primary_untouched).
claims.why: References external test file and TaskAttempt; not verifiable in this chunk.

claims.text: gate_concurrent_writes: Advisory-only tasks are bounced (this method only accepts write-mode work; use plan/accept for routing verdict on mixed tasks, or dispatch to actually run them).
claims.why: The method body is incomplete; cannot verify this behavior.

observations.what: The module docstring makes broad claims about system roles (Adam, Ikarus) and behavior that are not directly implemented in this chunk.
KairosScheduler.__post_init__ loads project data and policy from external modules (load_project, load_policy) which are not defined in this chunk. The behavior depends on those modules.
KairosScheduler.accept relies on route_and_select from provider_router, which is imported but not defined in this chunk. The routing logic is opaque.
KairosScheduler.dispatch calls offload from offload module, which is not defined in this chunk. The actual execution and safety guarantees depend on that external function.

The docstring of dispatch contains extensive claims about write concurrency hazards and isolation mechanisms that reference external modules (offload, gated_writes, TaskAttempt) not present in this chunk.
gate_concurrent_writes method is incomplete (truncated at end of chunk). Its full implementation and claims cannot be assessed.
The code uses ThreadPoolExecutor for parallel dispatch but the thread safety of _run_one (which calls offload) is not guaranteed by this chunk.
